definition: Tracking and segmenting a target object throughout a video, usually initialized from a first-frame mask or points.
details: Tracking and segmenting a target object throughout a video, usually initialized from a first-frame mask or points.

explainer.lead: Video Object Segmentation tracks and segments a target object throughout a video. It matters because it keeps an object's pixel-level outline consistent across frames, not just in one image.

tiers.eli5: You point at one thing in the first frame, and the system draws around that same thing in every later frame.
tiers.practitioner: The task is usually initialized from a first-frame mask or points, and the system must carry that target through the sequence. The pitfall is that everything downstream depends on that initial mask or point set being right.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as tracking and segmenting a target object throughout a video, usually initialized from a first-frame mask or points. No formulas, benchmarks, or numeric limits are specified.

explainer.example: A user supplies a mask around one person in the first frame, and the system segments that person in every subsequent frame.

usedIn.name: Mask-based tracking
usedIn.detail: initialized from first-frame masks or points
